tagline: Mechanistic pruning experiments for separating compression that preserves general perplexity from compression that preserves reasoning circuits.
phase_status: Phase 25 Validation: full auxiliary reasoning check complete
research_question: Where is the Mistral-7B GSM8K reasoning-retention boundary under tensor-preserving masks, and why does layerwise allocation outperform a standard global magnitude threshold?

overview.title: What we're building
overview.body: A structured pruning + activation healing pipeline (TIM-MGDT) that identifies which transformer layers and MLP widths are elastic, critical, or reasoning-specific. The current focus is Mistral-7B compression that survives GSM8K rather than merely preserving C4 perplexity.

overview.title: Why this matters
overview.body: Phase 16 showed the central failure mode: 20% hardware-aligned width pruning kept C4 perplexity in a plausible range but collapsed 5-shot GSM8K from 38.7% to about 5%. That is a useful negative result because it separates general language retention from reasoning-circuit retention.

overview.title: Where we are today
overview.body: Phase 25 full auxiliary scaling complete. Uniform structural width pruning collapses GSM8K even at 1%, while tensor-preserving masks expose a much higher-retention boundary. The strongest positive control is Mistral 20% layerwise mask sparsity with 37.2% full GSM8K versus 38.7% dense; the standard 20% global magnitude baseline reaches 35.3%, confirming retention but showing layerwise allocation matters. The full auxiliary check leaves the 20% layerwise mask statistically indistinguishable from dense on GSM8K Platinum and BBH multistep arithmetic.

decisions.rationale: We shifted focus to Mistral-7B and Llama-3-class architectures, where compression failures are meaningful for modern reasoning deployments.
Phase 18B and Phase 19 now form a controlled contrast: C4-matched structural and masked models can have very different GSM8K retention.
To ensure theoretical FLOP reductions translate to physical speedups, we round pruned MLP dimensions to nearest 64 (Tensor Core alignment) via specific ceil/floor strategies.

tasks.next_action: 20% layerwise mask full GSM8K is strong at 37.2% strict EM versus 38.7% dense. The standard 20% global magnitude mask reaches 35.3%, weaker than layerwise by 1.9 points but far above 20% structural width pruning.

Dense-revert probes from the 25% layerwise mask are close to the same-prefix no-revert baseline at n=300: no-revert is 36.0%, while single-group reverts range from 37.0% to 40.0% with overlapping confidence intervals. Report this as null or weak recovery at coarse granularity, not a localization claim.
Global unstructured magnitude pruning at 20.06% actual linear sparsity reaches 35.33% strict EM on full GSM8K with C4 PPL 8.203.
Initial mask-guided structural pruning failed: 0.45% and 0.89% MLP sparsity reached only 24% and 10% GSM8K smoke, so larger points are stopped by default.

The 20% mask is statistically indistinguishable from dense on the full auxiliary check: 39.95% vs 38.79% on GSM8K Platinum and 33.60% vs 32.40% on BBH multistep arithmetic, with overlapping confidence intervals.
Llama-3-8B GSM8K smoke is near dense at 10% mask sparsity (49% vs 53%, n=100) but drops at 20% (29%), so the Mistral 20% safe point should not be reported as universal.

Use COLM Efficient Reasoning as the technical target, but confirm remote or proxy presentation before committing to that venue because the workshop page says hybrid while the COLM FAQ is in-person-first.

milestones.description: Phase 12: Proxy validation, Memory Wall proof
Phase 14: Final pipeline execution (Mistral-7B LoRA healing)
Phase 15: True Layer Dropping and Boundary Healing
Phase 16: Hardware-aligned width pruning failed GSM8K despite plausible C4 PPL
Phase 17/18: Contrastive and non-uniform probes failed smoke tests
Phase 18B: Uniform structural sparsity sweep proved low-sparsity fragility
Phase 19: 20% dense-shaped mask preserves full GSM8K within 1.4 points of dense
Phase 20: initial mask-guided structural pruning failed smoke; use it as a negative control, not the method claim
Phase 25: full auxiliary reasoning check leaves the 20% layerwise mask statistically indistinguishable from dense on GSM8K Platinum and BBH multistep arithmetic
Phase 22: Llama-3-8B smoke suggests a lower model-specific safe threshold, with 10% near dense and 20% degraded
Phase 23: 20% global unstructured magnitude mask retains substantial GSM8K reasoning but trails the layerwise 20% mask
Phase 24: grouped dense-revert ablation shows no statistically distinguishable single-group recovery over the same-prefix 25% no-revert baseline
COLM Efficient Reasoning workshop submission, gated on confirmed remote/proxy presentation policy

bulletproofing.item: Multi-GPU OOM errors structurally prevented by parallelizing inference and sequentializing gradient bounds.
C4 perplexity, throughput, and full GSM8K metrics extracted for Phase 16.
20% mask pruning completed full GSM8K validation within 1.4 points of dense.
20% global unstructured magnitude baseline completed full GSM8K validation at 35.33% strict EM.
Grouped 25% dense-revert smoke completed with a same-prefix no-revert baseline and bootstrap confidence intervals.
Develop a structural method that preserves the Phase 19 mask-retained reasoning subspace while creating real speedups.

path_to_paper.item: Phase 19: Full GSM8K confirmed the 20% mask-vs-structural control.
Phase 16: Established the negative result: 20% MLP width pruning drops GSM8K from 38.7% to roughly 5%.
Phase 17/18: Keep the smoke-test failures as evidence, but do not invest more full-eval compute in those exact variants.
Tighten `paper/main.tex` around the Phase 23 global baseline: global 20% retained substantial reasoning, layerwise 20% remained stronger, and structural 20% collapsed.
Fold the Phase 24 grouped ablation into the paper as a smoke-level null/weak recovery diagnostic, not a strong localization claim.
Email the COLM Efficient Reasoning organizers to confirm whether accepted workshop contributions can be presented remotely or by proxy.
Final paper review and submission to the strongest venue whose presentation policy is compatible with travel constraints.
